/v/gaming just feels like a very rules heavy subverse to me. For a while it seemed like a lot of posts were just asking them to ban this or ban that. People over there would rather ban stuff than post content or have conversations. Just look at the sidebar, it's already crazy. A lot of those rules don't even mean anything specific (no clickbait? I'll probably still read /v/gaming now and then, but I probably won't be checking it every day like with other subs, and if I have a gaming link to share I probably won't be sharing it on /v/gaming.

Who is to say what are bad qualities and what are good? I had someone suggest to me that the 'Recently Viewed' items box was a bad quality of Reddit. Personal preference, I know, but in that person's mind this was a 'bad' quality.

While I understand and maybe even agree with you, I also see the flip-side. Reddit was home to a lot of us for years, and there's so much we love about it. It's not an accident that this place looks so similar to Reddit, even though there's plenty of style choices that could be made differently for an aggregator site. But the bad qualities have become too much to suck up. So we're here now. For better or worse, that's happening and it's going to keep happening as they continue to pile on the bad over there. And yeah, it's really hard to fight the temptation to bring over good things from Reddit... because we enjoyed them.. and feel others will too. And honestly, some things should be brought over and some shouldn't.

It's not an easy "DON'T MAKE VOAT LIKE REDDIT" situation... because no matter how you cut it Voat is a spawn of Reddit. Things have been taken from it from the beginning and will continue to be as long as there are things to take. Let's all just hope and pray that more good things come than bad.
